sources.fact: UK companies dataset covers registered land/property owned by UK companies or corporate bodies and excludes private individuals, overseas companies and charities.
CCOD is published monthly, contains title number/tenure/property address/proprietor/company registration number fields, and HMLR does not validate company registration numbers.
OCOD covers completed records of non-UK corporate ownership, with monthly complete/change-only files and known address/company-number inconsistencies.
OCOD title number is a relational key to other HMLR datasets; private individuals and several excluded owner classes are not represented.
HMLR title register provides title number, owner and rights information; title plan shows general boundaries.
Search by postcode, street/town, map or title number; unregistered land will not return ownership information from the register.
A title is an up-to-date legal-ownership record, but one title may comprise several plots/properties and does not necessarily expose every ownership interest.
HMLR Use land and property data API exposes ccod, ocod and National Polygon Service dataset metadata/resources.
National Data Library points to HMLR ownership data and notes National Polygon Service provides indicative shapes under licence.
Companies House public company information is free and can also be accessed by API for real-time company updates.
HMLR lists monthly company ownership datasets and monthly INSPIRE/NPS-related products with distinct legal/geospatial semantics.
HMLR portfolio reports can provide title number, property address, tenure and ownership information for a named company; this is company-portfolio evidence, not parcel boundary proof.

examples.result: CCOD/OCOD title number may be used as a join key only when the candidate's exact title relation is established.
Missing CCOD/OCOD record is not evidence of no owner because excluded/private/unregistered/pending cases exist.
Company Registration Number is cross-checked against Companies House; HMLR warns it may be missing or erroneous.
Company name similarity never substitutes for exact company number/title relation.
Title register owner evidence is distinguished from title-plan general-boundary geometry.
A single title may contain multiple plots/properties, so title identity is not automatically candidate-site identity.
Monthly publication cadence does not prove a candidate-specific ownership query was executed.
No candidate promotion occurs without exact title/site relation plus current planning/statutory evidence.
